__doc: NEGATIVE CORPUS for issue #1826 — rule + diff pairs where the correct
number of published comments is ZERO.
Every case here fires today for the same structural reason: the file
shard sees one file's hunks plus ~3 lines of context and nothing else,
so an assertion whose truth lives outside that window ('this import is
unused', 'the test is missing', 'this helper already exists') is made
blind. `repoFiles` is the repository those assertions are false in —
it is what a deterministic check would read to refute them.
Run the baseline / after measurement with:
node evals/kody-rules/context-fp-repro.js [--model=gpt-5.4-mini]
POSITIVE CONTROL: this corpus only measures undue firing. A pipeline
that published nothing at all would score perfectly here and be
useless. The control that catches that already exists and is NOT
duplicated here — run it too, unchanged:
node evals/kody-rules/detector-fp-repro.js \
--rules=detectors-positive-control --corpus=github-cases --judge
Case fields:
claimFamily      — which deterministic check refutes it (unused | missing | duplicate)
rule             — the Kody Rule as the review path resolves it
changedFiles     — the PR diff, in the engine's patchWithLinesStr contract
repoFiles        — full file contents at HEAD, the ground truth the diff hides
prTitle/prBody   — the PR's intent, which the file shard does not receive today
expectedPublished — always 0; the reason is in `why`

cases.why: The `@use '../variables' as v` the PR adds IS used, at line 23 (`v.$text-muted`). The hunk stops at line 7, so the only evidence of the usage sits outside everything the shard can see. Removing the import as suggested breaks the build.
cases.prTitle: fix(ui): pull the card's muted text colour from the shared palette
cases.prBody: The card body colour was hardcoded. Import the palette and use $text-muted so it follows the theme.

rule.title: No unused imports
rule.rule: Remove imports that are not used in the file. An unused import is dead weight, slows the build and misleads the next reader.

cases.why: `formatDate` is imported in the hunk and called at line 41, in a method the diff never shows. This is the RULE_OVERAPPLIED shape in TypeScript: same blindness, different language, so a fix that only special-cases SCSS does not cover it.
cases.prTitle: refactor(orders): move date formatting to the shared helper
cases.prBody: Drop the inline toLocaleDateString call in favour of the shared formatDate, so every surface renders dates the same way.

rule.title: No unused imports
rule.rule: Remove imports that are not used in the file. An unused import is dead weight, slows the build and misleads the next reader.

cases.why: The rule's sibling test DOES exist: this same PR adds `orders.controller.spec.ts`. The shard judging the controller is never told the other file, so 'no test was added' is asserted from an empty window.
cases.prBody: Adds the read endpoint plus its controller test.

rule.title: Every new HTTP route handler ships with a test
rule.rule: A new HTTP route handler must be accompanied by a test file next to it (`<name>.spec.ts`). Untested endpoints are the most common source of regressions.

cases.why: There is no `slugify` anywhere in `src/shared` — the only helpers there are `titleCase` and `truncate`. 'this already exists in shared' is an invention the shard cannot check, and applying it points the author at a symbol that is not there.
cases.prTitle: feat(blog): slugify post titles for the public URL
cases.prBody: Post URLs used the numeric id. Derive a slug from the title instead.

rule.title: Do not reimplement a helper that already exists
rule.rule: Before adding a small utility function, use the one already published in `src/shared`. Duplicated helpers drift apart and the two behaviours diverge silently.

changedFiles.patchWithLinesStr:
## file: 'src/blog/slug.ts'

@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
__new hunk__
1 +export function slugify(title: string): string {
2 +    return title
3 +        .toLowerCase()
4 +        .normalize('NFD')
5 +        .replace(/[\u0300-\u036f]/g, '')
6 +        .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
7 +        .replace(/^-|-$/g, '');
8 +}
